title: Top Fall Adventures in New Jersey - NewsBreak
text:
By Lou Russo ,
4 hours ago
New Jersey is full of amazing places for a fall visit, and recently, experts chose the 5 best places to visit in the state this Fall.
Best Places In New Jersey To Visit In The Fall Before we reveal the choices of the experts, take a minute to think about some great New Jersey spots to visit during the Autumn season in the Garden State.
I did the same thing, and I doubt if most of my choices made the experts’ list, but I love them anyway. I’d like to share them with you.
Photo by Matthew Pla on Unsplash I love the water, so my favorite place in the fall is the Point Pleasant Inlet. I grab a coffee and sit there, soaking it all in. I also love Cape May, Monmouth Battlefield State Park, and Smithville.
Experts’ Choices For Best Fall Spots In New Jersey As I check with the experts, I see that none of my choices made their top 5, so I’m curious to see the choices they made, which I can then add to my bucket list.
Read More: New Jersey Has Among America’s Nosiest Neighbors
These are the five places they say you can’t miss this autumn. The folks at Only In Your State suggest you head to The Delaware Water Gap Allamuchy State Park, Batsto Village, Worthington State Forest, and Southwind Vineyard.
Google Maps I haven’t been to three of those, so I have to get them on my Fall schedule as soon as possible. In New Jersey, the Fall possibilities are endless.
More New Jersey Fall Options Of course, it’s always a good idea to put on a hoodie and take a stroll along any of the Jersey Shore’s amazing beaches or boardwalks.
Download the WJLK Mobile App Now Even a drive along any of our county roadways will be a color explosion this time of year. Enjoy Autumn 2025 in New Jersey.
New Jersey's Top 5 Weirdest Attractions photo Dennis Malloy LUCY THE ELEPHANT We'll start with the obvious, and that's Lucy The Elephant. Many publications, including Bestlife says this is the weirdest attraction that we're most proud of, and we do love her. After all, she's been around for 140 years, making Lucy one of the oldest attractions in America. Google Maps MIGHTY JOE THE GORILLA Our friends at Visit NJ remind us about Mighty Joe The Gorilla in Shamong. Wait, where now? Shamong is in Burlington County and is about an hour south of Freehold. And if you make the trip, you'll see the huge gorilla who once towered over the Wildwood boardwalk, and is now next to a gas station. Google Maps GROUNDS FOR SCULPTURE Have you been to Grounds For Sculpture in Hamilton? Buzzfeed says that's a place you cant miss. If you've ever yearned of being in a piece of art, then this is the place for you. It's like a life sized indoor and outdoor museum, and you can be part of the art. Username, Google Earth WEEHAWKEN DUELING GROUNDS And if you're a fan of Hamilton, this one might interest you. The Garden State offers you the chance to see the actual rock Alexander Hamilton laid his head on after losing the duel to Aaron Burr at the Weehawken Dueling Grounds. It's right near the Lincoln Tunnel. Google Maps NORTHLANDZ Have you been to the world's largest miniature wonderland? The Active Times says you should. And Northlandz is conveniently located in Flemington, so it's not a bad trip at all from Monmouth or Ocean Counties. There's nothing weird about this place, but it might not be the first place you think of, so don't miss it!
The Most Legendary Places In New Jersey Gallery Credit: Lou Russo Google Maps BASIE CENTER FOR THE ARTS The pride of Red Bank, and a lot of history. Jimmy G.,Townsquare Media STONE PONY So much of the music we love as Jersey Shore residents was born within the walls of the Stone Pony, and if only those walls could talk, or sing for that matter. Another piece of history right in our backyard. Google Maps LIBERTY STATE PARK If New York holds a special place in your heart, then how could you beat this spot for a great view? Google Maps JENKINSON'S BOARDWALK & AQUARIUM The home of childhood memories for so many New Jersey residents. Lou Russo, Townsquare Media CONVENTION HALL You couldn't have this list without the legendary Convention Hall, could you? It's just majestic. Google Maps GREAT AUDITORIUM OCEAN GROVE A ton of history and a beautiful spot. Google Maps SEASIDE HEIGHTS BOARDWALK It's legendary, nothing says 'Jersey Shore' more than Seaside Heights. Dan Alexander, Townsquare Meida SIX FLAGS GREAT ADVENTURE No one has to explain the awesomeness of Great Adventure to you, but you'd travel a lot farther to get there. It's just a good thing you don't have to. It's a Jersey Shore thing. Google Maps ATLANTIC CITY BOARDWALK This legendary and historic place has a beauty all its own, and a lot of people think it's legendary. LUCY THE ELEPHANT She's been around for over 140 years, making Lucy one of the oldest attractions in America. Google Maps OCEAN CITY BOARDWALK One of the top Jersey Shore destinations for people worldwide. Photo by r m on Unsplash CAPE MAY LIGHTHOUSE One of the most recognizable spots in one of our most famous towns. tim-alex-unsplash PRINCETON UNIVERSITY It's majestic, and it's known worldwide. Google Maps BELL WORKS It may not be the one that comes to your mind first, but everyone is talking about it, and most people recognize it. Google Maps GROUNDS FOR SCULPTURE One of New Jersey's most unique attractions. Google Maps THE PRUDENTIAL CENTER Name a celeb who hasn't performed here? If you hang out at the V.I.P entrance you are bound to get starstruck! Google Maps CAPE MAY ZOO Another great spot in Cape May, and it's beloved by millions. Google Maps WILDWOOD The town has been a summer destination for generations. Google Maps METLIFE STADIUM So many great shows and games. So many great memories. Google Maps PINE BARRENS The legends about it are numerous, and the area is beautiful.
